coverage: 21 source fixtures, five relation modes, first A→B, immediate repeated A→B, B→A, A→A; full diagnostics, native ternaries and observed before/after state. The source specification declares setup cache entries and each mode's first-call work class.
endpoints: Setup includes source semantic graph, per-mode checker creation and A/B declared-type lookup, with before-lookup and before-first-action state recorded separately. The relation interval includes all four actions and their lazy resolution. Separate setup/relation requested traffic and live backing. Keep graph/results alive at after-checkpoints; raw before/after endpoint recording is mandatory.
execution: Fresh checker per mode; resolve source types immediately before that group. Lookup may populate relation caches and must satisfy each fixture's declared starting_cache_entries and setup class. Preserve that state without clearing caches. Display and independent diagnostic validation follow, outside relation timing. The first call is not necessarily cold, lazy, allocating or a cache hit.
forbidden: sealing/pre-resolving lazy graphs to bypass relation allocations
new unsafe, lifetime transmute or leaked graph storage
implementations: tools/s08/relater-prototype: isolated stable arena reference/interior mutability algorithm
proof: P1 records safe construction and mutation scopes, retained graph/result ownership and failure behavior before building the full reference alternative.

sampling.fixed_work: one ordered pass of all fixture/mode groups per fresh process; aggregate separately measured setup and relation intervals. If timer resolution is inadequate, report unavailable and review a protocol amendment before collecting comparison results; no result-dependent repeat count.
sampling.stability: Same max/min > 1.10 flag and complete-batch retention as checker-workload.json; no selective omission or automatic extension

scope: Supplemental isolated relater contract; never changes E2 primary denominator
state_comparison: Boolean and ternary outcomes, ordered diagnostics, cache flag multisets, declared setup/starting state and first/repeat creation/resolution transitions. Classification metadata in tools/s08/contracts/relations.json is validated against the frozen observations. Do not infer cache hits from existing entries or require every relation to allocate. Do not compare raw native TypeIds. Native type/signature/instantiation counts are semantic diagnostic expectations; explain any representation-only count difference explicitly rather than normalizing it silently.
verdict: Parity first, then one complete measured comparison. An unfavorable valid result meets the experiment obligation, but does not authorize production promotion.

first_call_classes.cold_lazy_resolution: All relation caches start empty; the first action increases at least one type, signature or instantiation counter. Preserve this lazy work inside the relation interval.
first_call_classes.cold_cache_evaluation: All relation caches start empty; the first action records relation cache entries without type/signature creation or instantiation counter growth. This is real relation work without a lazy allocation requirement.
first_call_classes.uncached_shortcut: All relation caches start empty and the first action leaves observed state unchanged; no cache-hit or lazy-work claim.
first_call_classes.primitive_identity_shortcut: flow-return-inference and jsdoc-module resolve A and B to number during setup. Lookup populates one assignable-cache entry, but every subsequent number-to-number action succeeds without changing counters or caches. These are semantic setup/identity fixtures, not cache-hit or cold-lazy evidence.
